_comment: HISTORICAL ORIGIN-IP SWEEP (wp_origin_history.py). Every A/AAAA record any collector has ever seen for a host (CIRCL/COF passive DNS, HackerTarget, SecurityTrails history, Validin, urlscan's hostname index, Webamon's servers index, passive-SSL cert->IP) is merged into ONE list, and each address is classified: `origin` (a plausible box the operator rented — worth an IP pivot), `cdn` (a shared CDN / WAF / DDoS-protection edge — its tenants are strangers), `parking` (a registrar/aftermarket parking farm), or `bogon` (non-routable). Only `origin` addresses are collected as IP seeds by the loop and the harness. The CIDR index (cdn_ranges.json) catches the providers that publish ranges; the groups below catch the edge networks that do NOT (Akamai, Imperva, Sucuri, DDoS-Guard …) by the ASN / org name the history source itself reported. A generic VPS/cloud ASN (OVH, Hetzner, DigitalOcean, AWS EC2, Linode) is deliberately NOT here: a rented VPS is exactly the origin this sweep exists to find, and shared hosting on it is caught downstream by the co-tenant count guard (noise_filters.shared_hosting_max_cohosts), not by provider name.

edge_asns._comment: ASN -> edge provider. An address whose history row (or IPPivot lookup) names one of these ASNs is a shared edge, never an origin. Only networks that run NOTHING BUT edge/WAF/scrubbing service belong here — an ASN that also sells VPS (Akamai Connected Cloud AS63949, G-Core, Datacamp/CDN77 AS60068) must stay out or real origins on it are discarded. Keys are 'AS<number>'.

edge_org_markers._comment: Case-insensitive WHOLE-WORD names in the org / ASN-name string a history source reports. Used when the source gives a name but no ASN. Keep to names that are unambiguously edge-only: never bare 'akamai' (Linode VPS now reports 'Akamai Connected Cloud' — only the CDN's legal names below), never 'amazon'/'google'/'microsoft' (their compute is real origin space; their CDN ranges are in cdn_ranges.json).

parking_markers._comment: Case-insensitive WHOLE-WORD names in the org / ASN-name of domain-PARKING and aftermarket farms ('sedo' matches 'Sedo GmbH', never 'Sedona Hosting'). A parked or for-sale era answers on an address shared by millions of parked names — never an operator origin, and usually the previous owner's or the registrar's era, not this operator's.

ambiguous_asns._comment: ASN -> provider for networks that sell BOTH DDoS-protection proxying AND plain VDS/dedicated hosting (DDoS-Guard, StackPath/Highwinds). An address there may be a shared protection edge (other customers behind it) or the operator's own rented box — both are common for scam infrastructure. Classified `ambiguous`: the IP IS collected (ASN, abuse contact, ports, certificates are evidence either way) but its co-tenants are ALWAYS held as leads, never seeded, and no domain->IP clustering edge is written.

ambiguous_org_markers._comment: Whole-word org / ASN-name markers for the same proxy-or-host networks as ambiguous_asns, used when a history source gives a name but no ASN.

ad_edge._comment: AD-NETWORK / AD-CDN EDGE on a hyperscaler (seen live: an Ezoic-fronted site answering on a rotating set of Amazon AS16509 addresses in many regions at once). One host that resolves, within `window_days` of its most recent sighting, to at least `min_ips` addresses on one of `asns` (or inside `region_cidrs`) spread across at least `min_regions` distinct regions is NOT an operator box: it is the ad network's edge pool, shared by every publisher on that network. All those rows are reclassified `cdn` (provider `provider`) so they are never collected as IP seeds and never write a hosted_on edge — two unrelated publishers on the same ad network must never cluster. `region_cidrs` is a curated subset of the largest EC2 prefixes per region from https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json (service EC2, refreshed 2026-10-18); an AS16509 row outside them still counts toward `min_ips`, but only a CIDR hit names a region. Provider-level data only (RULE 1).

no_owner_verdict._comment: DETERMINISTIC VERDICT for IP-only clusters (harness/orchestrator.py run_case_parallel). A judged cluster whose members are only IPs (plus provider hostnames) where EVERY address classifies as one of `class_confidence`'s keys, and no member carries an owner-rung signal, gets a fixed `inconclusive` verdict instead of an LLM assess phase. `class_confidence` is the confidence of that inconclusive judgment per class (the cluster takes the lowest of its members'); a class missing here sends the cluster to the LLM. Classes: cdn / parking / bogon (origin-history classification), ad_edge (the ad_edge rule above), shared-hosting (the box answers for more than noise_filters.SHARED_HOSTING_MAX_COHOSTS sites), platform (a noise-flagged hosting network answering for more than sweep_policy.vps_auto_max_cotenants sites — a small VPS is a plausible operator box and goes to the LLM). `provider_host_suffixes`: hostnames under these are the provider's own names (default PTRs, edge names, parking hosts), never an operator asset. `benign_ip_pivot_kinds`: the only IP-raw pivot kinds that are NOT an owner signal (an ip:ptr under a provider suffix is benign too; a certificate, self-hosted MX, misconfig leak or distinctive PTR is not). `owner_pivot_prefixes`: pivot kinds on a provider hostname's raw that are owner-rung (rungs.json owner classes).

sweep_policy._comment: Breadth of the sweep. `max_ips_per_host`: origin addresses one host may contribute to the frontier per round (ranked live-first, then by how many independent sources saw it, then most recent). `max_ip_seeds_per_round`: origin IPs the loop collects per round across the whole case. `recent_tenancy_days`: an address the case host has NOT used within this many days is a HISTORICAL origin — still collected (its ASN, ports, PTR and certificates are evidence), but its CURRENT co-tenants may have moved in after our host left, so they are held back as leads instead of seeded. `vps_auto_max_cotenants`: on a recent origin whose network the IP lookup flags as cloud/VPS hosting (Google Cloud, DigitalOcean, OVH, Hetzner, Vultr …), up to this many co-hosted apexes are queued as neighbours and linked to the IP automatically; above it they become an analyst-approval lead that lists EVERY domain, and nothing is collected or linked until approved.
